vocabulary.meaning: 形容词：敌对的；怀有敌意的
名词：坚持不让步的人；唯一反对者
形容词：醉酒的，酒精中毒的
名词：合理怀疑（法律上足以阻止定罪的疑问）
短语：一眨眼，极短的时间
名词：悖论，自相矛盾的情况

subtitles.en: Good to be with you.
subtitles.zh: 很高兴和大家见面。

subtitles.en: I'm Tony Dokoupil.
subtitles.zh: 我是托尼·多库皮尔。

subtitles.en: The breaking news right now.
subtitles.zh: 现在为您插播突发新闻。

subtitles.en: Banning the press.
subtitles.zh: 封禁媒体。

subtitles.en: I don't have to let them into the people's house.
subtitles.zh: 我不一定非得让他们进白宫。

subtitles.en: TONY DOKOUPIL: THE president kicking three news organizations out of the White House.
subtitles.zh: 总统把三家新闻机构赶出白宫。

subtitles.en: What they're saying tonight.
subtitles.zh: 他们今晚如何回应。

subtitles.en: And can he do this?
subtitles.zh: 他有权这样做吗？

subtitles.en: Air emergency.
subtitles.zh: 空中紧急状况。

subtitles.en: The burned out cabin where a battery pack burst into flames hours into an overseas flight.
subtitles.zh: 海外航班飞行数小时后，电池组突然起火，客舱被烧毁。

subtitles.en: What to know about the danger as more passengers bring devices onto planes.
subtitles.zh: 随着越来越多乘客带电子设备上飞机，你需要了解这些危险。

subtitles.en: CBS News exclusive Patrick Clancy and what he wants the world to know following the killing of his three children.
subtitles.zh: CBS新闻独家：帕特里克·克兰西在三个孩子遇害后，想告诉世界什么。

subtitles.en: I live with the outcome.
subtitles.zh: 我承受着这个结果。

subtitles.en: I live with it every day.
subtitles.zh: 我每天都活在其中。

subtitles.en: TONY DOKOUPIL: Our conversation with the 60 Minutes correspondent who got the interview as the lone holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial breaks his silence.
subtitles.zh: 我们采访了《60分钟》的记者，他采访到了林赛·克兰西谋杀案中唯一坚持反对意见的陪审员，这名陪审员打破了沉默。

subtitles.en: What he is now saying about his vote.
subtitles.zh: 他现在对自己的投票怎么说。

subtitles.en: Plus, the first interview with Princess Diana's brother after his accusations against the royal family.
subtitles.zh: 另外，戴安娜王妃的弟弟在指控王室后首次接受采访。

subtitles.en: What he said about King Charles and Prince Harry.
subtitles.zh: 他谈到了查尔斯国王和哈里王子哪些内容。

subtitles.en: A mountain lion on the loose roaming the streets of San Francisco.
subtitles.zh: 一头美洲狮在旧金山街头游荡。

subtitles.en: What happened next?
subtitles.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

subtitles.en: Hero dog.
subtitles.zh: 英雄犬。

subtitles.en: The celebration for a police canine recovering after an on the job injury.
subtitles.zh: 一只警犬因公受伤后康复，人们为它庆祝。

subtitles.en: And tonight, Steve Hartman shows us when you're a parent, the days may be long, but the years are short.
subtitles.zh: 今晚，史蒂夫·哈特曼带来：为人父母，日子虽长，岁月却短。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: Why is it so hard then?
subtitles.zh: 那为什么这么难熬呢？

subtitles.en: You reduce in size in their rear view mirror, but they stay the same for you.
subtitles.zh: 你在他们的后视镜里越来越小，但他们在你眼里始终没变。

subtitles.en: ANNOUNCER: From CBS News headquarters in New York.
subtitles.zh: 这里是纽约 CBS 新闻总部。

subtitles.en: This is the CBS Evening News with Tony Dokoupil.
subtitles.zh: 这里是 CBS 晚间新闻，我是托尼·多库皮尔。

subtitles.en: And good evening.
subtitles.zh: 各位晚上好。

subtitles.en: President Trump today claimed he is banning a trio of major media companies from the White House, continuing a long, hostile relationship with the press.
subtitles.zh: 特朗普总统今天声称，他正在禁止三家大型媒体进入白宫，延续了他与新闻界长期敌对的关系。

subtitles.en: But while he claimed on social media that the ban on CNN, MSNOW, and Politico was effective immediately, there was no immediate follow through aside from a new round of the same old name calling inside the White House.
subtitles.zh: 不过，尽管他在社交媒体上声称对 CNN、MSNOW 和 Politico 的禁令立即生效，但除了白宫里又一轮老套的辱骂外，并没有立即采取后续行动。

subtitles.en: And as with past attempts to block coverage, he may lose this one in court.
subtitles.zh: 和过去试图阻止报道的做法一样，这一次他可能会在法庭上败诉。

subtitles.en: We get the latest now from our Weijia Jiang at the White House.
subtitles.zh: 现在请本台驻白宫记者姜伟嘉带来最新报道。

subtitles.en: WEIJIA JIANG: Tonight President Trump is defending his decision to ban CNN, Politico, and MSNOW from the White House.
subtitles.zh: 今晚，特朗普总统为禁止 CNN、Politico 和 MSNOW 进入白宫的决定进行辩护。

subtitles.en: A very simple ban.
subtitles.zh: 非常简单的禁令。

subtitles.en: I don't want them in my office.
subtitles.zh: 我不想让他们进我的办公室。

subtitles.en: I don't want them here.
subtitles.zh: 我不想让他们在这里。

subtitles.en: I would say the ban would go as far as you can.
subtitles.zh: 我想说，这个禁令会尽可能从严执行。

subtitles.en: WEIJIA JIANG: Trump first made the announcement on social media, claiming the outlet shouldn't be able to constantly write or report fiction and lies when they are covering the President of the United States.
subtitles.zh: 特朗普最初是在社交媒体上宣布这一决定的，他声称这些媒体在报道美国总统时，不应该不断编造和报道虚构内容与谎言。

subtitles.en: They purposely write negative news, and they do that because they want to try and diminish the Republicans in a Republican administration.
subtitles.zh: 他们故意写负面新闻，这么做是想在共和党执政期间削弱共和党人。

subtitles.en: And honestly, we've done a fantastic job.
subtitles.zh: 说实话，我们做得非常好。

subtitles.en: WEIJIA JIANG: Trump has a history of attacking the press.
subtitles.zh: 特朗普素来喜欢攻击新闻界。

subtitles.en: Fake news doesn't report those stories.
subtitles.zh: 假新闻不报道那些事。

subtitles.en: Boy, that's a lot of fake news.
subtitles.zh: 天哪，那有好多假新闻。

subtitles.en: WEIJIA JIANG: And female reporters in particular.
subtitles.zh: 尤其是对女记者。

subtitles.en: You're a loud, boisterous person.
subtitles.zh: 你是个大嗓门、吵吵嚷嚷的人。

subtitles.en: You're fake news.
subtitles.zh: 你是假新闻。

subtitles.en: Be quiet.
subtitles.zh: 安静。

subtitles.en: That's enough.
subtitles.zh: 够了。

subtitles.en: Put down the mic.
subtitles.zh: 把话筒放下。

subtitles.en: WEIJIA JIANG: He's also tried to restrict the media before.
subtitles.zh: 他以前也试图限制媒体。

subtitles.en: In his first term, he revoked Jim Acosta's White House credential and barred Kaitlan Collins from an event.
subtitles.zh: 在第一任期内，他吊销了吉姆·阿科斯塔的白宫记者证，并禁止凯特兰·柯林斯参加一场活动。

subtitles.en: Both were reporters for CNN.
subtitles.zh: 两人当时都是 CNN 的记者。

subtitles.en: Last year, he kicked the Associated Press out of the Oval Office events because the outlet refused to use Trump's chosen name, "the Gulf of America."
subtitles.zh: 去年，他把美联社赶出了椭圆办公室的活动，因为该媒体拒绝使用特朗普选定的名称“美国湾”。

subtitles.en: This ban will likely be challenged in court.
subtitles.zh: 这项禁令很可能会在法庭上受到挑战。

subtitles.en: I think every time the president explains why he thinks this ban is necessary, it's actually worse for his legal case because he keeps talking about negative coverage and unfair coverage.
subtitles.zh: 我认为，每次总统解释为什么他认为这项禁令是必要的，对他的法律案件来说实际上都更不利，因为他不断提到负面报道和不公平报道。

subtitles.en: And again, that's what the First Amendment protects against.
subtitles.zh: 再说一次，这正是第一修正案所要防范的。

subtitles.en: In fact, in all those previous cases, access was restored to members of the press after legal battles.
subtitles.zh: 事实上，在之前所有那些案件中，媒体成员在法律斗争后都恢复了采访权。

subtitles.en: This evening, reporters from all three of the outlets Trump just threatened are here at the White House doing their jobs.
subtitles.zh: 今晚，特朗普刚刚威胁的这三家媒体的记者都在白宫正常工作。

subtitles.en: And tell us they have not been asked to leave.
subtitles.zh: 他们告诉我们，目前没有人要求他们离开。

subtitles.en: Tony.
subtitles.zh: 托尼。

subtitles.en: Weijia, you know this train well.
subtitles.zh: 伟佳，你对这行再熟悉不过了。

subtitles.en: You were president of the White House Correspondents' Association.
subtitles.zh: 你曾担任白宫记者协会主席。

subtitles.en: You understand the relationship between this White House and the press corps.
subtitles.zh: 你了解这届白宫和记者团之间的关系。

subtitles.en: What do you make of it all?
subtitles.zh: 你对此怎么看？

subtitles.en: That's right.
subtitles.zh: 没错。

subtitles.en: Tony, the Association is used to plenty of tension as we advocate for access.
subtitles.zh: 托尼，协会在争取采访准入时，早就习惯了各种紧张关系。

subtitles.en: But while Trump has gone after reporters before, this is different because he may ban entire outlets from White House grounds.
subtitles.zh: 不过，虽然特朗普以前也针对过记者，但这次不同，因为他可能会禁止整个新闻机构进入白宫场地。

subtitles.en: That's an escalation from keeping folks out of the Oval Office or off of Air Force One.
subtitles.zh: 这比把记者挡在椭圆形办公室外或不让上空军一号又进一步升级了。

subtitles.en: Tonight, the WHCA says in a statement that the Constitution protects the freedom of the press from government interference, and that is ultimately for the good of the American public, Tony.
subtitles.zh: 今晚，白宫记者协会在一份声明中表示，宪法保护新闻自由不受政府干预，这归根结底是为了美国公众的利益，托尼。

subtitles.en: Weijia, thank you very much.
subtitles.zh: 伟佳，非常感谢。

subtitles.en: Also today, President Trump announced a new deal with Greenland after threatening to take the island, citing US security concerns.
subtitles.zh: 同样在今天，特朗普总统宣布与格陵兰达成一项新协议；此前他曾以美国安全关切为由，威胁要接管该岛。

subtitles.en: The president said the agreement granted the US "permanent control over Greenland's security and all other needs."
subtitles.zh: 总统表示，该协议赋予美国“对格陵兰安全及所有其他需求的永久控制权”。

subtitles.en: Denmark, which handles the island's foreign policy, said the deal will be signed next week.
subtitles.zh: 负责该岛外交政策的丹麦表示，协议将于下周签署。

subtitles.en: A battery pack burst into flames yesterday hours into a flight from Amsterdam to Curacao, forcing the pilot, who was already out there over the ocean, to turn back toward land.
subtitles.zh: 昨天，在从阿姆斯特丹飞往库拉索的航班起飞几小时后，一个电池组突然起火，迫使已经在海洋上空的飞行员掉头飞回陆地。

subtitles.en: Tonight, we're getting our first look at the damage.
subtitles.zh: 今晚，我们首次看到了受损情况。

subtitles.en: CBS's Tom Hanson joins me now with the pictures and a warning for flyers.
subtitles.zh: CBS 的汤姆·汉森现在带来这些画面，并要给乘客提个醒。

subtitles.en: Hey there, Tony.
subtitles.zh: 嗨，托尼。

subtitles.en: Good evening to you.
subtitles.zh: 晚上好。

subtitles.en: Well, some scary moments on a flight from Amsterdam yesterday after a power bank caught fire as the plane was over the Atlantic Ocean.
subtitles.zh: 昨天从阿姆斯特丹起飞的航班上发生了一些惊险时刻：飞机在大西洋上空时，一个充电宝起火。

subtitles.en: Just take a look at some of these images.
subtitles.zh: 大家来看看其中一些画面。

subtitles.en: The incident charred the window shade and injured one passenger who suffered minor burns.
subtitles.zh: 事故烧焦了遮光板，并造成一名乘客轻微烧伤。

subtitles.en: The flight was headed to Curacao, but, of course, diverted back to Amsterdam.
subtitles.zh: 该航班原定飞往库拉索，但后来当然改航返回了阿姆斯特丹。

subtitles.en: Now, lithium battery fires are a known issue and have been on the rise since 2020.
subtitles.zh: 锂电池起火是一个已知问题，自 2020 年以来一直在增加。

subtitles.en: The FAA says there have been 77 incidents this year, 40 from battery packs, and just last month, firefighters had to rush on board an American flight in Dallas after reports of several passengers being burned when a laptop caught fire.
subtitles.zh: 联邦航空管理局表示，今年已发生 77 起事件，其中 40 起由电池组引起；就在上个月，在达拉斯一趟美国航空航班上，有报道称一台笔记本电脑起火，多名乘客被烧伤，消防员不得不冲上飞机。

subtitles.en: Now, earlier this year, the FAA showed CBS News the testing it's doing looking for ways to reduce the danger of these fires in the cabin.
subtitles.zh: 今年早些时候，联邦航空管理局向 CBS 新闻展示了他们正在进行的测试，目的是寻找减少客舱内此类火灾危险的方法。

subtitles.en: The battery demos CBS saw burnt the cameras, and another test burnt a hole through the chair's seatback.
subtitles.zh: CBS 看到的电池演示烧毁了摄像机，另一次测试把座椅靠背烧穿了一个洞。

subtitles.en: The FAA giving us this guidance.
subtitles.zh: 联邦航空管理局给出了以下建议。

subtitles.en: If you notice that your device is overheating or getting hot to the touch, it is starting to swell or smoke, immediately call the flight attendant and they will fight that fire.
subtitles.zh: 如果你发现设备过热或摸起来发烫，开始鼓包或冒烟，请立刻呼叫空乘，他们会来灭火。

subtitles.en: And the FAA strictly requires that anything with a lithium ion battery go in your carry on luggage.
subtitles.zh: 联邦航空管理局严格要求，任何含锂离子电池的物品都必须放在随身行李中。

subtitles.en: That includes vapes and personal devices.
subtitles.zh: 这包括电子烟和个人电子设备。

subtitles.en: The FAA also telling us that a fire on a plane is the worst case scenario, Tony.
subtitles.zh: 联邦航空管理局还告诉我们，飞机上起火是最糟糕的情况，托尼。

subtitles.en: Really is.
subtitles.zh: 确实是。

subtitles.en: Tom, thank you.
subtitles.zh: 汤姆，谢谢。

subtitles.en: And in Los Angeles today, the driver who crashed into that metro bus earlier this week arrived in court on a stretcher wrapped in blankets to face second degree murder charges.
subtitles.zh: 在洛杉矶，本周早些时候撞上那辆公交巴士的司机今天躺在担架上、裹着毯子出庭，面临二级谋杀指控。

subtitles.en: Officials say she was intoxicated and driving against traffic.
subtitles.zh: 官员们称她当时醉酒，并且逆行驾驶。

subtitles.en: And to make things worse, a news helicopter covering the deadly accident also crashed, killing two on board and a pedestrian on the ground.
subtitles.zh: 更糟的是，一架正在报道这起致命事故的新闻直升机也坠毁了，机上两人和地面一名行人遇难。

subtitles.en: Now to a CBS News exclusive.
subtitles.zh: 接下来是 CBS 新闻的独家报道。

subtitles.en: Our conversation with Patrick Clancy and his new wife, Dr. Rachel Dinis.
subtitles.zh: 我们与帕特里克·克兰西及其新婚妻子蕾切尔·迪尼斯医生的对话。

subtitles.en: 60 Minutes correspondent Ross Douthat interviewed the couple about the case against Patrick's ex-wife, Lindsay Clancy, whose trial, of course, for the killing of their three small children ended earlier this month without a verdict.
subtitles.zh: 《60分钟》记者罗斯·多塞特采访了这对夫妇，谈及帕特里克前妻林赛·克兰西的案件。她因杀害三个年幼的孩子受审，审判本月早些时候结束，但没有做出裁决。

subtitles.en: Patrick, for the first time since then, is taking questions on all of it.
subtitles.zh: 帕特里克在那之后首次就这一切接受提问。

subtitles.en: ROSS DOUTHAT: Are you angry at yourself?
subtitles.zh: 罗斯·多塞特：你生自己的气吗？

subtitles.en: Do you feel like you failed in some way in this period?
subtitles.zh: 你是否觉得自己在那段时期里有什么地方没做好？

subtitles.en: Or do you feel like you did the best you could?
subtitles.zh: 还是觉得自己已经尽了最大努力？

subtitles.en: I think I did the best I could with what I had at the time.
subtitles.zh: 我觉得在当时的条件下，我已经尽了最大努力。

subtitles.en: And I live with the outcome.
subtitles.zh: 而我承受着这个结果。

subtitles.en: I live with it every day, but I think I did the best I could.
subtitles.zh: 我每天都承受着它，但我认为我已经尽了最大努力。

subtitles.en: And joining me now is 60 Minutes correspondent Ross Douthat.
subtitles.zh: 现在加入我们的是《60分钟》记者罗斯·多塞特。

subtitles.en: Ross, great to have you here.
subtitles.zh: 罗斯，很高兴你来做客。

subtitles.en: Great to be here.
subtitles.zh: 很高兴能来。

subtitles.en: What can we expect from the piece on Sunday?
subtitles.zh: 周日的报道我们可以期待哪些内容？

subtitles.en: I think the biggest thing is just a portrait of Patrick's life in the aftermath of this incredible tragedy, and what it's like to deal with that kind of grief, that kind of unimaginable experience as a father, and then what it means to try and rebuild your life in the shadow of that experience and try and go forward from there.
subtitles.zh: 我认为最重要的是：它描绘了帕特里克在这场令人难以置信的悲剧之后的生活，以及作为一名父亲要面对那种悲伤、那种难以想象的经历是什么感受，还有在那段经历的阴影下努力重建生活、继续往前走意味着什么。

subtitles.en: Why do you think Patrick Clancy wanted to do this interview?
subtitles.zh: 你认为帕特里克·克兰西为什么想接受这次采访？

subtitles.en: I think from the beginning, he's been focused on trying to make sure that the memory of his children stays alive and stays close to the center of this story.
subtitles.zh: 我认为从一开始，他就一直专注于让孩子们不被遗忘，始终留在这个故事的中心。

subtitles.en: And obviously, there's been so many debates, so much controversy about all of the different issues around this story.
subtitles.zh: 显然，围绕这个故事的各种问题有太多争论、太多争议。

subtitles.en: Mental health, marriage, men and women, the medical system, all of these things.
subtitles.zh: 心理健康、婚姻、男人和女人、医疗系统，所有这些。

subtitles.en: And there have been all kinds of, obviously, online accusations against Patrick himself.
subtitles.zh: 而且显然，网上对帕特里克本人也有各种各样的指控。

subtitles.en: And he felt his kids, Cora, Dawson, and Callan, were getting lost in all that noise and he wanted to put the spotlight back on them.
subtitles.zh: 而他觉得他的孩子科拉、道森和卡伦正在被这些噪音淹没，所以他想把聚光灯重新放回他们身上。

subtitles.en: And so it is.
subtitles.zh: 确实如此。

subtitles.en: Ross, thank you very much.
subtitles.zh: 罗斯，非常感谢。

subtitles.en: Thank you.
subtitles.zh: 谢谢。

subtitles.en: We'll have Ross Douthat's full exclusive report on 60 Minutes this Sunday.
subtitles.zh: 本周日，《60分钟》将播出罗斯·多塞特的完整独家报道。

subtitles.en: And tonight we're also hearing from the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder case.
subtitles.zh: 今晚我们还将听到林赛·克兰西谋杀案中唯一坚持己见的陪审员的说法。

subtitles.en: The defense had argued that Clancy lost all control suffering from postpartum psychosis when she killed her three children.
subtitles.zh: 辩方此前主张，克兰西在杀害三个孩子时因产后精神病完全失控。

subtitles.en: The juror, however, says she knew exactly what she was doing.
subtitles.zh: 然而这位陪审员说，她完全清楚自己在做什么。

subtitles.en: Our Shanelle Kaul reports.
subtitles.zh: 本台记者沙内尔·考尔报道。

subtitles.en: SHANELLE KAUL: The holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial has broken his silence.
subtitles.zh: 林赛·克兰西谋杀案审判中唯一坚持己见的陪审员已经打破沉默。

subtitles.en: In a statement obtained by CBS News through his representative, Michael Desronvil says, I didn't have any doubts.
subtitles.zh: CBS新闻通过其代表获得的一份声明中，迈克尔·德斯龙维尔说：“我没有任何怀疑。”

subtitles.en: As I tried to explain different possible theories during deliberation, I kept getting cut off as if I had doubts based on the evidence present.
subtitles.zh: 在评议期间，我试图解释各种不同的可能性，却不断被打断，好像我是根据现有证据产生了怀疑。

subtitles.en: Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses, and what the prosecution presents, I thought it was enough proof that she knew exactly what she was doing and planned.
subtitles.zh: 基于所有物证、关键证人和检方出示的内容，我认为这足以证明她完全清楚自己在做什么，而且是蓄意为之。

subtitles.en: He had said he had doubt.
subtitles.zh: 他之前曾表示自己有怀疑。

subtitles.en: SHANELLE KAUL: Paula Devlin says she was one of the 11 jurors who wanted Lindsay Clancy to be found not criminally responsible, and told us she believes the holdout juror wasn't following the law when it came to reasonable doubt.
subtitles.zh: 葆拉·德夫林说，她是希望认定林赛·克兰西不承担刑事责任的11名陪审员之一。她还告诉我们，她认为那位坚持己见的陪审员在合理怀疑问题上没有依法行事。

subtitles.en: If he had shown us some evidence, then we all would have been OK with that.
subtitles.zh: 如果他当时给我们看了任何证据，我们都会接受。

subtitles.en: But you don't feel like that's what happened here?
subtitles.zh: 但你觉得这里的情况不是那样？

subtitles.en: Unfortunately, no.
subtitles.zh: 遗憾的是，并不是。

subtitles.en: Whose word matters more here?
subtitles.zh: 在这里，谁的话更管用？

subtitles.en: The holdout juror or the 11 jurors.
subtitles.zh: 是坚持己见的那位陪审员，还是11名陪审员？

subtitles.en: The holdout juror.
subtitles.zh: 坚持己见的那位陪审员。
百分之百。

subtitles.en: Otherwise, we could have a chilling effect on the process of jury deliberations.
subtitles.zh: 否则，可能对陪审团评议过程产生寒蝉效应。

subtitles.en: The holding out really is a testament to what the jury deliberation process should look like.
subtitles.zh: 这种坚持己见恰恰证明，陪审团评议过程本应如此。

subtitles.en: After the mistrial Desronvil was targeted online.
subtitles.zh: 审判无效后，德斯龙维尔在网上遭到攻击。

subtitles.en: He hired a defamation lawyer, and the state, meantime, has not yet announced if it will retry Lindsay Clancy.
subtitles.zh: 他聘请了一名诽谤律师；与此同时，州政府尚未宣布是否会重新审判林赛·克兰西。

subtitles.en: Tony.
subtitles.zh: 托尼。

subtitles.en: Shanelle, thank you very much.
subtitles.zh: 沙内尔，非常感谢。

subtitles.en: And as we've been reporting, some of the most powerful people in the AI industry are filled with worry, even dread over what might go wrong.
subtitles.zh: 正如我们一直在报道的，人工智能行业一些最有权势的人对可能出问题的情况充满担忧，甚至恐惧。

subtitles.en: But NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang is not one of those people.
subtitles.zh: 但英伟达创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋不在此列。

subtitles.en: He sat down with our Jo Ling Kent for an exclusive interview, arguing that now is not the time to slow down.
subtitles.zh: 他接受了本台记者乔玲·肯特的独家专访，认为现在不是放慢脚步的时候。

subtitles.en: So should we slow down, and would that affect the race with China?
subtitles.zh: 那么我们应该放慢速度吗？那会影响和中国的竞争吗？

subtitles.en: We should go as fast as we can, irrespective of anybody else.
subtitles.zh: 我们应当尽可能快地推进，不管别人怎么做。

subtitles.en: We're going to go as fast as we can, but we would never, ever and never should ship products before they're ready, deliver products that are unsafe, and nobody's expecting us to do that.
subtitles.zh: 我们会尽可能快地推进，但绝不会在产品准备好之前就发布，绝不会交付不安全的产品，也没人期望我们那样做。

subtitles.en: But everybody's expecting us to succeed and help America be as prosperous as possible.
subtitles.zh: 但所有人都期待我们成功，并帮助美国尽可能繁荣。

subtitles.en: You can see more of Jo Ling Kent's exclusive report with NVIDIA CEO this weekend on CBS Sunday Morning.
subtitles.zh: 本周末，您可以在CBS《周日早间》看到乔玲·肯特对英伟达首席执行官的更多独家报道。

subtitles.en: Still ahead on the broadcast tonight, a mountain lion on the loose and a quite literally wild chase on the streets of San Francisco.
subtitles.zh: 今晚节目稍后：一头山狮出逃，旧金山街头上演了一场名副其实的疯狂追逐。

subtitles.en: Just two blocks North of the San Francisco Zoo, a mountain lion from the wild this morning terrorized the neighborhood.
subtitles.zh: 就在旧金山动物园以北两个街区，今天早上，一头野生山狮惊扰了附近居民。

subtitles.en: Carter Evans now with details.
subtitles.zh: 卡特·埃文斯带来详细报道。

subtitles.en: CARTER EVANS: It's a wild police chase with a fugitive feline on the streets of San Francisco.
subtitles.zh: 在旧金山街头，警方对一只在逃的猫科动物展开了疯狂追捕。

subtitles.en: MAN: Coming our way.
subtitles.zh: 朝我们这边来了。

subtitles.en: JENSEN HUANG: But this mountain lion appears to have a problem with authority ignoring police containment lines.
subtitles.zh: 但这头山狮似乎对权威有意见，无视警方的封锁线。

subtitles.en: I thought they were exaggerating when they said we needed to get out of the way before.
subtitles.zh: 之前他们说我们得让开，我还以为他们太夸张了。

subtitles.en: But they were right.
subtitles.zh: 但他们没错。

subtitles.en: [LAUGHS] It was just so fast.
subtitles.zh: （笑）它实在是太快了。

subtitles.en: MAN: It's beautiful.
subtitles.zh: 真美。

subtitles.en: CARTER EVANS: The animal was spotted this morning in a residential neighborhood and quickly became a media sensation.
subtitles.zh: 今天早上，这只动物在居民区被发现，并迅速成为媒体焦点。

subtitles.en: REPORTER: Breaking news out of San Francisco, where a mountain lion has been spotted hiding under a bush.
subtitles.zh: 旧金山突发新闻：有人发现一头山狮藏在灌木丛下。

subtitles.en: CARTER EVANS: He's not lying.
subtitles.zh: 他没说谎。

subtitles.en: There it is.
subtitles.zh: 就在那儿。

subtitles.en: A terrifying sight for neighbors.
subtitles.zh: 邻居们看到这一幕都吓坏了。

subtitles.en: My primal instincts kicked in and I ran.
subtitles.zh: 我的原始本能被激发出来，拔腿就跑。

subtitles.en: CARTER EVANS: Even the mayor took to social media.
subtitles.zh: 就连市长也到社交媒体上发声。

subtitles.en: So just avoid the area, and we will keep you posted.
subtitles.zh: 请大家避开那一带，我们会持续更新情况。

subtitles.en: CARTER EVANS: The chase finally ended with an unplanned cat nap.
subtitles.zh: 这场追逐最终以一次意外的“猫打盹”收场。

subtitles.en: Wildlife officers tranquilized the mountain lion and carried it to safety.
subtitles.zh: 野生动物管理人员给这头山狮注射了镇静剂，把它转移到安全地方。

subtitles.en: MAN: There it is, guys.
subtitles.zh: 就是它，各位。

subtitles.en: CARTER EVANS: The cougar culprit in custody.
subtitles.zh: 这头美洲狮肇事者已被控制。

subtitles.en: Now, you may have noticed authorities with their arms up, almost as if they were trying to catch the mountain lion.
subtitles.zh: 您可能注意到，工作人员举着双臂，几乎像是在准备接住那头山狮。

subtitles.en: And it may look absurd, but that's exactly what wildlife experts say you should do.
subtitles.zh: 这看起来也许有点滑稽，但这正是野生动物专家建议做的。

subtitles.en: Hold up your arms, look big, and definitely do not turn and run, because that could trigger the lion's instinct to chase.
subtitles.zh: 举起手臂，让自己显得高大，千万不要转身跑，因为这可能触发狮子的追逐本能。

subtitles.en: Tony.
subtitles.zh: 托尼。

subtitles.en: Carter, thank you very much.
subtitles.zh: 卡特，非常感谢。

subtitles.en: When a police officer arrived at a major fire in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, early Sunday and heard that a young family was still inside.
subtitles.zh: 周日清晨，威斯康星州欧克莱尔发生一场大火，一名警察到场后听说，一户年轻家庭仍困在里面。

subtitles.en: He did not go looking for a firefighter.
subtitles.zh: 他没有去找消防员。

subtitles.en: He went right in himself, warned the family, and even scooped up a baby to help everyone get out and with no injuries.
subtitles.zh: 他自己直接冲了进去，提醒了那家人，还抱起一个婴儿，帮助所有人安全逃出来，而且没有人受伤。

subtitles.en: Big cheers today for a police canine in Utah just released from the vet.
subtitles.zh: 犹他州一只警犬今天从兽医那里出院，大家为它欢呼。

subtitles.en: This is Bruno, who broke both legs on the job investigating a suspicious package with the Park City Police Department.
subtitles.zh: 这是布鲁诺，它在为帕克城警察局调查一个可疑包裹时，两条腿都骨折了。

subtitles.en: But he is now on the mend and reunited with his family.
subtitles.zh: 但它现在正在康复，并且和家人团聚了。

subtitles.en: Up next on the road with Steve Hartman confronts the question that every parent eventually faces.
subtitles.zh: 接下来，史蒂夫·哈特曼的《在路上》将面对每个父母最终都会遇到的问题。

subtitles.en: Where did all the time go?
subtitles.zh: 时间都去哪儿了？

subtitles.en: Finally tonight on the road where for a change, Steve Hartman stays home and for a reason every parent can relate to.
subtitles.zh: 今晚最后的《在路上》里，这次不同以往，史蒂夫·哈特曼待在家里，原因每个父母都能理解。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: It happened to my wife, Andrea, and me after our first child was born, and it happened constantly.
subtitles.zh: 这件事在我第一个孩子出生后，就发生在我和妻子安德烈娅身上，而且经常发生。

subtitles.en: Do you remember the advice that pretty much everybody gave us when we first had George?
subtitles.zh: 你还记得我们刚有了乔治时，几乎每个人都给我们的建议吗？

subtitles.en: Oh my gosh, it goes so fast.
subtitles.zh: 天哪，时间过得真快。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: Cherish this.
subtitles.zh: 珍惜这段时光。

subtitles.en: It goes so fast.
subtitles.zh: 时间过得真快。

subtitles.en: Yeah.
subtitles.zh: 是啊。

subtitles.en: And I could not imagine it going fast.
subtitles.zh: 我当时无法想象它会过得很快。

subtitles.en: No, and now it feels like a blink of an eye.
subtitles.zh: 对，现在感觉就像一眨眼。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: For us, that 18 year blink just happened.
subtitles.zh: 对我们来说，那18年就像一眨眼，刚刚过去。

subtitles.en: George is starting college, and although we have taught him everything he needs to know to live independently, except maybe how to pack a t-shirt.
subtitles.zh: 乔治要开始上大学了，虽然我们已经教会了他独立生活所需的一切，除了也许怎么叠T恤。

subtitles.en: I suppose I'll figure that out.
subtitles.zh: 我想我会自己弄明白的。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: No one ever taught us how to deal with his vacancy.
subtitles.zh: 从来没有人教过我们如何面对他离开后的空缺。

subtitles.en: How to get past this most puzzling parenting paradox.
subtitles.zh: 怎么熬过这个最令人困惑的育儿悖论。

subtitles.en: He annoys us sometimes now.
subtitles.zh: 他现在有时候也会让我们烦。

subtitles.en: Yeah, I think all children do.
subtitles.zh: 是啊，我觉得所有孩子都会。

subtitles.en: We annoy him.
subtitles.zh: 我们也会惹他烦。

subtitles.en: We annoy him immensely.
subtitles.zh: 我们让他烦得不行。

subtitles.en: [LAUGHS] Yeah.
subtitles.zh: [笑] 是啊。

subtitles.en: Why is it so hard then?
subtitles.zh: 那为什么这么难呢？

subtitles.en: You send your kids off to college, and you reduce in size in their rear view mirror.
subtitles.zh: 你把孩子送去上大学，你在他们的后视镜里就变小了。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: Yeah.
subtitles.zh: 是啊。

subtitles.en: But they stay the same for you.
subtitles.zh: 但他们在你眼里还是老样子。

subtitles.en: As parents, I think you just imagine your kids are always going to be there until one night there's an empty spot at the dinner table.
subtitles.zh: 作为父母，我觉得你会一直以为孩子总会在身边，直到某个晚上餐桌旁空出一个位置。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: In preparation for that moment, every couple of years I interviewed my kids, hoping to capture that time as it flew by.
subtitles.zh: 为了给那一刻做准备，我每隔几年就采访我的孩子们，希望能捕捉住飞逝的时光。

subtitles.en: From those early days of steely confidence.
subtitles.zh: 从那些透着坚定自信的早年时光开始。

subtitles.en: What do you want to be when you grow up?
subtitles.zh: 你长大后想做什么？

subtitles.en: Chemist or an astrophysicist.
subtitles.zh: 化学家或天体物理学家。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: Through the tender times of his first crush.
subtitles.zh: 经历他第一次心动时的温柔时光。

subtitles.en: What makes her special?
subtitles.zh: 她有什么特别之处？

subtitles.en: Her liking me back, honestly, is what makes that really special.
subtitles.zh: 老实说，她也喜欢我，这才是真正特别的地方。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: I even have those memorable years that hardly seem worth remembering.
subtitles.zh: 我甚至还留着那些几乎不值得记住、却又难忘的岁月。

subtitles.en: They say that sometimes when kids hit puberty, they get moody.
subtitles.zh: 他们说孩子进入青春期后，有时会变得情绪化。

subtitles.en: Whatever.
subtitles.zh: 随便吧。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: I have saved it all.
subtitles.zh: 我把这些都保存了下来。

subtitles.en: Unfortunately, documenting the passage of time doesn't change our perception of it.
subtitles.zh: 遗憾的是，记录时间的流逝并不会改变我们对它的感受。

subtitles.en: No matter how many photos you take or videos you record, it's still over in an instant.
subtitles.zh: 无论你拍多少照片、录多少视频，它还是在一瞬间就结束了。

subtitles.en: George left for school earlier this month.
subtitles.zh: 乔治这个月早些时候离家去学校了。

subtitles.en: He'll major in math.
subtitles.zh: 他将主修数学。

subtitles.en: And as for us remainders, I'm doing OK.
subtitles.zh: 至于我们这些留下来的人，我还好。

subtitles.en: But my wife-- well, it's going to take her a little longer to adjust.
subtitles.zh: 但我妻子——嗯，她需要更长一点时间来适应。

subtitles.en: And not only because she misses him.
subtitles.zh: 而且不只是因为她想他。

subtitles.en: How much of it do you think is you're just worried about having to spend more time with me?
subtitles.zh: 你觉得有多少是因为你担心以后要和我在一起待更久？

subtitles.en: Big part.
subtitles.zh: 很大一部分。

subtitles.en: STEVE HARTMAN: Steve Hartman from an "emptier nest" in New York.
subtitles.zh: 史蒂夫·哈特曼，来自纽约一个“更空的巢”。

subtitles.en: Steve Hartman on what he calls "the 18-year blink."
subtitles.zh: 史蒂夫·哈特曼谈他所说的“18年一眨眼”。

subtitles.en: Thank you, Steve.
subtitles.zh: 谢谢你，史蒂夫。

subtitles.en: That's another day in America.
subtitles.zh: 这就是美国的又一天。

subtitles.en: I'm Tony Dokoupil.
subtitles.zh: 我是托尼·多库皮尔。

subtitles.en: For all of us here at CBS News, thank you for watching this week.
subtitles.zh: 我们CBS新闻全体同仁，感谢你本周收看。

subtitles.en: We'll see you right back here on Monday.
subtitles.zh: 我们周一在这里再见。

subtitles.en: Good night.
subtitles.zh: 晚安。
